overall: The AG found the Wareham School Committee failed to timely approve minutes for five meetings (Jan 15, Feb 5, Feb 26, Mar 5, Mar 19, 2026), ordered future compliance, and declined the broad audit and Town Charter allegations.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to timely approve open session minutes of meetings held between May 2025 and April 2026.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee failed to timely approve the minutes of the meetings held on January 15, February 5, February 26, March 5, and March 19 as the minutes were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the April 2, 2026 meeting were reviewed as part of the timeliness allegation.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes of the April 2 meeting were approved in a timely manner where the minutes were approved within three meetings as required by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes for all meetings from May 2025 to April 2026 were untimely approved, a broad audit-style request.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review whether all minutes of Committee meetings held during the eleven-month period between May 2025 and April 2026 have been timely approved as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee violated the Town Charter by failing to post meeting minutes on the town website.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government does not interpret municipal charters or bylaws nor does it review allegations that a Committee violated the town charter.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
